audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 1 Chronicles / Divrei Hayamim Aleph census, plague, angel, and Ornan threshing-floor narrative, first-pass restored draft with public-domain scaffold; later witness audit required
audit_status.review_note: Reviewed against 2 Samuel 24 for Satan/YHWH agency contradiction, census purpose and numbers, Joab's refusal, collective punishment, famine/war/plague choice, seventy-thousand deaths, stopping command, David's responsibility, sheep metaphor, Ornan and sons, coerced land transaction, price variants, altar fire, and David's fear.

verses.restored: An adversary/Satan stood against Israel and incited David to count Israel.
David said to Joab and rulers of people, Go, count Israel from Beersheba to Dan, and bring number to me so I may know it.
Joab said, May YHWH add to people a hundred times. My lord king, are they not all servants of my lord? Why does my lord seek this? Why should it become guilt for Israel?
King's word prevailed over Joab. Joab went throughout all Israel and came to Jerusalem.
Joab gave total count to David: all Israel, one million one hundred thousand sword-drawing men; Judah, four hundred seventy thousand sword-drawing men.
Levi and Benjamin he did not count among them, for king's word was abhorrent to Joab.
This matter was evil in eyes of Divine, and Divine struck Israel.
David said to Divine, I have sinned greatly by doing this; now remove guilt of servant, for I acted very foolishly.
YHWH spoke to Gad, David's seer, saying,
Go and speak to David: Thus says YHWH, Three things I offer you; choose one, and I will do it to you.
Gad came to David and said, Thus says YHWH, Choose for yourself:

three years of famine, three months swept away before foes while enemies' sword overtakes, or three days sword of YHWH—plague in land and messenger of YHWH destroying throughout Israel. Now consider what word I shall return.
David said to Gad, I am in great distress. Let me fall into hand of YHWH, for very great are mercies, but let me not fall into human hand.
YHWH sent plague upon Israel, and seventy thousand people of Israel fell.

Divine sent a messenger to Jerusalem to destroy it; as destruction occurred, YHWH saw and relented concerning harm and said to destroying messenger, Enough; now release your hand. Messenger of YHWH stood by threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite.
David lifted eyes and saw messenger of YHWH standing between earth and heavens, drawn sword in hand stretched over Jerusalem. David and elders, clothed in sackcloth, fell on faces.

David said to Divine, Was it not I who commanded people counted? I am one who sinned and did evil; these sheep, what have they done? YHWH my Divine, let your hand be against me and father's house, but not against your people as plague.
Messenger of YHWH told Gad to say to David that David should go up and establish altar to YHWH at threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite.
David went up according to word Gad spoke in name of YHWH.
Ornan turned and saw messenger; his four sons with him hid themselves. Ornan was threshing wheat.
David came to Ornan; Ornan looked, saw David, went out from threshing floor, and bowed to David with face to ground.
David said to Ornan, Give me site of threshing floor, that I may build altar to YHWH; for full price give it to me, so plague may be restrained from people.
Ornan said to David, Take it; let my lord king do what is good in his eyes. See, I give oxen for burnt offerings, threshing sledges for wood, and wheat for grain offering; I give all.
King David said to Ornan, No, for buying I will buy for full price; I will not take what is yours for YHWH or offer burnt offering without cost.
David gave Ornan for site six hundred shekels of gold by weight.
David built altar to YHWH there, brought burnt and well-being offerings, called to YHWH, and YHWH answered with fire from heavens upon altar.
YHWH commanded messenger, and messenger returned sword to sheath.
At that time, when David saw YHWH answered at threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite, he sacrificed there.
Dwelling of YHWH Moses made in wilderness and altar of burnt offering were then at high place in Gibeon.
David could not go before it to inquire of Divine, for he was terrified before sword of messenger of YHWH.

translation_notes: 2 Samuel 24:1 says YHWH incited David; 1 Chronicles 21:1 attributes incitement to an adversary/Satan. The contradiction must remain visible.
Counting people is not inherently sinful. Likely concerns include military conscription, taxation, royal possession, or distrust, but the text does not fully explain.
Joab's resistance is overridden by royal command, showing that a subordinate's ethical objection can be valid even when the objector is morally compromised elsewhere.
Famine, military defeat, and plague fall chiefly on ordinary people rather than the king who chose the census. Collective punishment is not justice.
Seventy thousand deaths may not become props for David's lesson or evidence that epidemics punish sin.
The clearest ethical command is 'Enough; release your hand.' Mercy interrupts destruction rather than glorifying it.
David calls people sheep; his admission of responsibility is important, but people are not royal property or passive livestock.
Ornan is a Jebusite landowner approached by a king during catastrophe. Bowing and offering everything do not prove free consent under extreme power imbalance.
Ornan's four sons hide from the angelic threat; child/family terror remains part of the site-acquisition story.
The price differs sharply from 2 Samuel 24:24; numbers, site scope, agency, and plague details require textual audit.
Fire from heaven and angelic imagery are not instructions for ritual technique, plague control, or violence.
safety_note: Reject epidemic-punishment theology, collective punishment, census superstition, coerced land transfer, angelic-war imitation, and leader-centered grief. Center the seventy thousand dead, terrified families, Joab's refusal, David's responsibility, Ornan's ownership, and the command: Enough—release your hand.
